Formulation
35-year-old male with untreated hypothyroidism presents with 3–6 month history of low mood, anergia, reduced appetite, weight loss, and episodic anxiety/panic sensations. Predisposing factors may include thyroid dysfunction and high-stress occupation. Precipitating factor appears to be recent job change. Symptoms are perpetuated by discontinuation of thyroxine and reduced activity. Protective factors include supportive spouse and engagement with care.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Regain energy and normal mood  
  • Resume normal appetite and marital intimacy
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Clarify diagnosis (depression vs thyroid-related)  
  • Improve mood and functional status within 3 months
- Actions (Patient):
  • Attend ordered blood tests promptly  
  • Resume/adhere to prescribed thyroid medication if advised  
  • Monitor mood, appetite, anxiety episodes; keep symptom diary
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Order comprehensive blood panel including thyroid function, FBC, metabolic profile, B12/folate  
  • Review results; if thyroid abnormal, initiate/adjust thyroxine  
  • Screen for depression (e.g., PHQ-9) at next visit; consider SSRI or psychotherapy referral based on results

Secondary Problem (Anxiety/Panic Episodes):
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce or eliminate elevator-related panic, palpitations, and breathlessness
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Determine if episodes meet criteria for panic disorder; reduce frequency/intensity
- Actions (Patient):
  • Record triggers, duration, and coping strategies for each episode  
  • Practice slow diaphragmatic breathing during episodes
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide brief psycho-education on panic physiology  
  • Offer referral for CBT focused on anxiety management if episodes persist

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: need for blood tests, potential thyroid contribution, when to seek urgent care for chest pain or bowel changes
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Further loss of appetite/weight, persistent low mood, increased panic frequency, emergence of suicidal thoughts
- Coping Strategies: Breathing techniques, maintaining activity as tolerated, symptom diary, engage support from wife

Consent, Coordination & Review

- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 3 months or sooner following blood test results
